po_authorization_ref: Executed under the existing D35 decision (T0075). No new Product-Owner architecture decision is created: the authoritative baseline is the already-approved FINAL contract and Phase-1A evidence.
previous_state_note: The first clean-install audit misattributed the cross-schema foreign key to iam_v2.pms_interfaces, queried pg_constraint for an object MG-0 creates as a unique INDEX, and therefore reported that the development appliance lacked the contract-defined anchor and had diverged from committed mg1. It also claimed an exact match to the appliance on the strength of a table count.
new_state_note: Both claims are RETRACTED. Re-queried read-only, the appliance carries guest_networks_tsi_anchor valid and ready with exactly the contract definition, and iam_v2.guest_network_pms_map carries the composite FK to public.guest_networks (tenant_id, site_id, id) -- precisely what the Phase-1A live-dark acceptance records. Nothing drifted and there are not two competing baselines. The clean-install path is now production-grade in the repository: the accepted IAM base and MG-0 are promoted into an ordered, ledger-recorded path before 0009, the IAM ownership roles come from deploy/gatep/gatep-iam-roles.sql instead of the scratch fixture, three service-created tables are declared by migration 0048, the reconstruction uses the appliance's own TimescaleDB image and the real Gate-P role and grant path, and a semantic comparison covering columns, constraints, indexes, triggers, functions, ownership, memberships and grants shows the structural surface IDENTICAL.
corrected_findings: RETRACTED: committed mg1 does not FK pms_interfaces to guest_networks. The anchor belongs to iam_v2.guest_network_pms_map (tenant_id, site_id, guest_network_id) -> public.guest_networks (tenant_id, site_id, id).

RETRACTED: the development appliance did not lose the anchor. MG-0 creates it as a unique INDEX and the earlier check queried pg_constraint, which cannot see one. guest_networks_tsi_anchor is present, valid and ready with the exact contract definition.
RETRACTED: 'matches the appliance exactly' rested on a table count and is replaced by a semantic catalog comparison.
CORRECTED: IAM base and MG-0 promoted to data-plane/migrations/iam_base/, applied between 0008 and 0009 and recorded in schema_migrations. iam_v2_scratch retained as provenance only.
CORRECTED: edge_executed_commands, edge_installed_updates and edge_offline_packages were created by scd at runtime and are now declared by migration 0048.
CORRECTED: iam_v2_owner and iam_v2_migrator promoted from the scratch fixture into deploy/gatep/gatep-iam-roles.sql.
CORRECTED: the reconstruction uses timescale/timescaledb:2.16.1-pg16, without which the hypertable insert-blocker triggers were silently absent.
remaining_blockers: OWNERSHIP: 26 iam_v2 objects created by migrations 0009+ are owned by the platform role in a clean build and by iam_v2_owner on the appliance. Those migrations must run as the platform role because they maintain public.schema_migrations. An explicit ownership-reassertion step is required before a production install, because ownership decides what the SECURITY DEFINER boundary functions execute as.

CONFIGURATION-SELECTABLE LEGACY AUTHORITY: treated as a Production-readiness blocker per the zero-superseded-active-dependency objective. The authority switch is call-level across six files, so legacy guest-auth remains compiled in and selectable by configuration. Per-object assessment recorded: guest_accounts, ticket_templates, vouchers, voucher_batches, sessions, auth_otps and guests are superseded; operators, operator_roles, tenants, sites, appliances, guest_networks, audit_log and accounting_records are retained platform foundations.
boundaries_observed: 172.21.60.23 NOT modified. Every query against it was read-only reference evidence.
No deployment to any server. No Production appliance exists or was contacted.
No historical migration, scratch file or governance evidence deleted.
The reconstruction ran in disposable containers on the workstation and copied no runtime state.
No capability enabled, no PMS, provider or financial traffic, two-NIC model and all permanent product rules preserved.
next: Product-Owner provision of the new Production server and access, plus a decision on the two remaining blockers: the ownership-reassertion step and the removal of the configuration-selectable legacy authority.
